event.canonical_title: Sen. Cassidy Supports Todd Blanche's Attorney General Confirmation
event.summary: Republican Senator Bill Cassidy has announced his support for Todd Blanche's nomination as attorney general, which is expected to facilitate Blanche's confirmation by the Senate. Cassidy's backing comes after two other Republican senators expressed their opposition to Blanche's nomination, making Cassidy's support crucial for moving forward.

timeline.title: Senate Confirms Todd Blanche as Attorney General Amid Controversy
timeline.summary: The Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as the new Attorney General with a narrow vote of 50-49 early Saturday morning. The confirmation followed a contentious process, with concerns raised about Blanche's ability to maintain independence from President Trump's influence over the Justice Department. Democrats criticized Blanche, labeling him an enabler of Trump's alleged corruption.

event_overview.title: About Sen. Cassidy Supports Todd Blanche's Attorney General Confirmation
event_overview.subject: Sen. Cassidy Supports Todd Blanche's Attorney General Confirmation
event_overview.summary: This event concerns the Senate’s consideration and confirmation of Todd Blanche to lead the U.S. Department of Justice as Attorney General after President Donald Trump nominated him for the office. Sen. Bill Cassidy’s stated support was part of the Senate confirmation process, which followed a Judiciary Committee hearing and a closely divided full-Senate vote.

facts.label: Nomination
facts.value: President Trump sent Blanche’s nomination to the Senate on June 8, 2026, to serve as Attorney General.

facts.label: Senate process
facts.value: The Senate Judiciary Committee held a nomination hearing for Blanche on July 15, 2026, in Room 216 of the Hart Senate Office Building in Washington, D.C.

facts.label: Confirmation
facts.value: The Senate confirmed Blanche as Attorney General by a 50–49 vote on August 8, 2026, according to Associated Press reporting.

facts.label: Office and responsibilities
facts.value: The Attorney General heads the Department of Justice, represents the United States in legal matters, and advises the President and executive departments; the office originated with the Judiciary Act of 1789 and later became the head of the Justice Department established in 1870.

facts.label: Prior role
facts.value: Before this nomination, Blanche was the 40th Deputy Attorney General and later served as Acting Attorney General; the Deputy Attorney General assists in directing Justice Department policy and operations and acts as Attorney General when that office is vacant.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers Cassidy’s support and the final confirmation developments on August 7–8, 2026, rather than every hearing exchange, endorsement, objection, or Justice Department action connected to the nomination.
